main_body: A flat 4x3-tile grass ground patch (64x48 px) with a repeating tuft pattern; terrain, not a standing object.
top_band: none (flat ground texture; the column scan shows only repeating green runs of 12 rows L=86 and 4 rows L=64, which are the tile pattern, not a top surface)
evidence: The candidate is a seamless ground texture, so the 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply. There is no standing volume and no side face. The column scan shows a repeating 16-row period of mid green with a dark green band, which is the tuft pattern. Nothing is drawn as a standing object that would fail as a front elevation.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and a median of 26 per tile. The ramp is shallow: a base green, a dark green and a light green, plus a few orange dots. The same 16x16 tile motif repeats mechanically, which reads as a stamped pattern and not as hand-shaded grass. There are no flat 5x5 fills, and the dark pixels are tinted green, not neutral. Texture and density are far below the Beodeul grass reference, so it looks thinner and flatter next to it.
